briefs.headline: Cabinet OKs 10,000 crore SME growth fund
briefs.deck: The Union Cabinet has approved the establishment of a Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund for small and medium enterprises. This initiative aims to provide equity, liquidity, and professional support to foster growth. Existing funds typically support early-stage micro enterprises, leaving a gap for SMEs needing growth capital. The fund will focus on enterprises in Tier II and Tier III industrial…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund (SGF), aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to enable the emergence of champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. The fund was announced in the last budget, focusing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem.
"There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly micro enterprises. A structural gap exists for equity growth capital for SMEs. The fund will consider SME's operating in industrial clusters in Tier II and Tier III cities," government said in a statement. It added that by providing long-term capital, the initiative will enable Indian SMEs to scale operations.

briefs.headline: 4G mobiles make a comeback on costlier 5G smartphones
briefs.deck: India is experiencing a noticeable slowdown in the shift to 5G smartphones due to rising costs. As a result, the demand for 4G devices is increasing, especially in the Rs 10,000-20,000 segment. More smartphone brands are now offering 4G models as consumers seek better specifications without the 5G price tag. Analysts indicate that this shift to 4G may persist as component costs remain high.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Costlier smartphones are slowing India's shift to 5G. Rising component costs are driving a comeback for 4G devices as buyers seek better specifications at affordable prices.
Shipments of 4G smartphones are expected to grow 3% in 2026 even as the overall market declines, according to Counterpoint Research. Their share of smartphone shipments is projected to rise from 11% in 2025 to 13% this year and 15% in 2027.
The shift is particularly visible in the Rs 10,000-20,000 segment, where the number of smartphone makers offering 4G models has increased from two in 2025 to 12 this year. "India's 4G recovery is increasingly extending beyond the traditional entry-level segment," Counterpoint senior analyst Prachir Singh said. Buyers in this price band are seeking better device experiences without the higher price associated with 5G, he added.
India's overall smartphone shipments fell 11% year-on-year in the June quarter, Counterpoint said, with record-high memory costs triggering multiple price hikes and weakening demand, particularly at the lower end.
"Building a 5G phone under Rs 15,000 that doesn't compromise on the overall experience has become extremely challenging," Sumit Singh, SVP and head of products at Lava International, told TOI. 
"At the same time, consumer purchasing power hasn't grown to match these rising costs."
Lava continues to prioritise 5G but has revisited its strategy for the sub-Rs 15,000 market. Demand, Singh said, is "not for the cheapest phone" but for better value, specifications and ownership experience. Brands like Xiaomi, Infinix, Realme have also launched 4G phones this year.
Counterpoint research director Tarun Pathak said the shift could outlast a temporary response to higher prices because component costs are unlikely to normalise quickly. For manufacturers, this creates room to offer better-equipped 4G devices at affordable prices, while buyers increasingly weigh connectivity against the overall experience. The trade-off is making 4G a broader value proposition beyond its traditional entry-level role.

briefs.headline: Volatility triggered by CAS surges on NSE on expiry day
briefs.deck: The Closing Auction Session faced volatility as weekly derivatives contracts expired in Indian markets. Nifty surged over 300 points and then dropped significantly while Sensex also fluctuated. This market movement occurred due to falling Brent crude oil prices and global market cues. Investors remained cautious ahead of the RBI policy decision on inflation and potential tightening.
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: After a break of about two weeks, Closing Auction Session (CAS) again played truant during Tuesday's late session as weekly derivatives contracts on 
NSE
 were expiring. Within a span of just 30 seconds-between 15:20:00 and 15:20:30-Nifty rallied a little over 300 points or about 1.5%, and in the next eight minutes fell about 240 points or 1.1%.
Sensex
 also saw a sudden spike but a relatively smaller one during CAS. The index rose about 350 points or 0.5% and then fell from the high. To address issues of CAS-related volatility, markets regulator Sebi is working on changing some rules for the session.
At the close of Tuesday's trading, sensex was up 685 points or 1% while 
Nifty
 closed 220 points or 1% up at 22,776 points. The gains in the indices, which marked the second consecutive day of rise, came on the back of falling Brent prices that went below the psychologically important $100/barrel level, along with strong global cues.
According to Vinod Nair, head of research, at Geojit Investments, crude oil prices slipped below the $100-mark after a large G7 stockpile release and alternative supply measures helped offset disruptions to vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz.
"Coupled with strong Q2 business updates from financials and retail along with supportive global cues, the decline in oil prices improved investors' sentiment and supported a rebound from the oversold levels. 
Domestically, attention now shifts to the Q2 earnings season for silver lining amid weak sequential expectations due to elevated input costs," Nair wrote in a note to investors.
Market players said Dalal Street investors would remain cautious ahead of the RBI policy decision on Wednesday, "with the focus firmly on the central bank's inflation outlook and guidance on further policy tightening," Nair said.
Interestingly, the day's gains in the two indices came despite Rs 2,961 crore worth of net selling by foreign funds in the stock market, BSE data showed. In contrast, domestic institutions were net buyers at Rs 5,089 crore.

briefs.headline: FMCG Q2: Margins under pressure
briefs.deck: Fast-moving consumer goods companies are experiencing increased commodity costs, alongside the impact of weak monsoons on consumption. Despite these challenges, companies are projecting revenue and volume growth for the quarter. However, analysts expect profitability pressures to continue, which may limit earnings surprises. Selective price hikes have negated some benefits from GST cuts in the…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are grappling with heightened commodity cost inflation amid a sharp rebound in crude oil prices while the impact of weak monsoons is slowly showing up in pockets of consumption, companies said in their Q2 updates even as they estimated strong revenue and volume growth for the quarter.
The broader takeaway is that demand continues to hold up but margins are under pressure. Analysts and brokerages attributed much of the growth to a mix of GST cut benefits, low base and selective price hikes, projecting a weak outlook for the sector going ahead.
The markets are mirroring the underlying pressure-FMCG Nifty Index is down nearly 16% since Jan 1. "With sustained cost headwinds, we may see growth moderation ahead, which alongside margin strain could stress FY27 earnings," analysts at HDFC Securities said in a note. Godrej Consumer Products (GCPL) flagged intensifying input cost pressures during the quarter and said that uneven monsoon conditions also weighed on consumption. "We are responding through a combination of calibrated pricing actions, cost-saving initiatives, supply chain efficiencies," GCPL said, estimating high-teens revenue growth and high single-digit underlying volume growth.
Dabur, which expects consolidated revenues to record double-digit growth, said that operating margins were impacted by inflationary pressures, partly offset by price increases.
"While volume trends have been stable so far (led by GST benefit and soft base), margin trajectory may not improve as expected with RM (raw material) pressures not abating. Hence, despite low double-digit sales growth, earnings growth is unlikely to be exciting or surprise positively for most of the names," analysts at JM Financial said.
The impact on volume growth will be visible from the March quarter, said independent consumer consultant Akshay D'souza. "The story in FMCG is that profitability is under pressure," D'souza said. Even as companies have refrained from passing on the full impact of commodity inflation to consumers so far, selective hikes have negated much of the benefits from reduced prices post GST cuts. Further price increases in the coming months cannot be ruled out.
"Domestic demand remained resilient during the quarter, even as the operating environment stayed volatile through the period. Looking ahead, we remain optimistic on consumption trends, while closely monitoring the evolving inflationary conditions," said Marico.

briefs.headline: E-way bills point to fertiliser diversion
briefs.deck: The introduction of the e-way bill has significantly improved the tracking of fertiliser movement across India. Preliminary checks during the fertiliser crisis revealed diversion of goods meant for designated locations. The government is keen to combat such activities, especially following the increased pressure on fertiliser prices. A parliamentary committee highlighted instances of leakage and…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The humble e-way bill, introduced to check truck movement nine years ago, has helped govt track diversion of fertiliser. Thanks to the electronic tool, which is to be used by every truck carrying goods valued at over Rs 50,000, just a preliminary check at the height of the fertiliser crisis post Iran war showed that trucks meant to deliver goods at designated locations were making detours or were making one trip too many.
"The ministry did some preliminary checks when, after the war started, there were concerns that there may be some fertiliser shortage and there were also fears of hoarding and diversion," an official said.
The finance ministry, which undertook the analysis, then alerted the fertiliser department. Diversion of fertiliser, which is highly subsidised, is not a new phenomenon but govt is more than keen to crack down on it in the wake of the renewed pressure on prices, although supply has eased and govt has stocked up. The fertiliser ministry also maintains Integrated Fertiliser Management System (iFMS) to track the movement of subsidised fertiliser.
A parliamentary standing committee recently noted that there was leakage during transportation. "Partial unloading and re-routing during transit from rake points to remote districts (particularly in hilly terrain - J&K, Uttarakhand); movement without valid documents (Madhya Pradesh: 28 cases of unauthorised movement in 2025-26); delayed or non-reporting of receipt at destination (were observed)," it said in a report tabled in Aug.
The parliamentary panel recently said that neem-coated urea was seeing diversion to industrial units such as plywood and resin factories, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) units and for cattle feed manufacturing, especially in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, and Punjab.
According to agriculture ministry data, in 2025, 4.8 lakh raids were conducted across the country and over 17,000 notices were issued, while nearly 7,000 licences were cancelled with 850-odd FIRs registered against defaulters.
In fact, there have been multiple studies by agencies which also point to smuggling of fertiliser from India to neighbouring countries through trucks.

briefs.headline: Most GST refunds may be processed within 17 days
briefs.deck: The GST Council intends to shorten the refund processing period to around 17 days for businesses. It will also work to automate registering for a GST number to speed up the process. For small businesses operating in multiple states, avoiding repetitive registrations will be considered. Additionally, the proposal includes eliminating physical verification for registration cancellations. Changes…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The GST Council, which meets Thursday, will seek to slash the refund period to around 17 days, which will include a maximum 10 days for acknowledgement, beyond which it will be deemed to have been acknowledged, and seven days for processing. Currently, acknowledgement itself can take 21-45 days and the idea is to process refunds faster, officials said Tuesday. Currently, around 90% of the refunds are processed quickly.
Similarly, the idea is to prune the time taken for registering for a GST number through a more automated process. While 61% of the registrations take place within three days, the plan is to automate processes so that the time taken for the remaining 39% of the applications is reduced from several days. But, officials also said that not all registrations take a long time as those for businesses below Rs 2.5 lakh turnover are given within 34 minutes on an average.
For small businesses that operate in more than one state, the GST Council will consider steps that will enable them to avoid the registration exercise across states if an e-commerce platform through which they sell has a recognised warehouse as a place of business. 
"Overall, nine out of 10 sellers on platforms will gain," an official said.
In case of an entity looking to cancel its registration, the Centre and the states will discuss a proposal to do away with the physical verification of the premises by an official, where the presence of the businessman is required. If taxes are paid and returns are filed, registration will be cancelled, an official said, adding that the idea is to move to a trust-based system.
Similarly, through a host of changes in the rules, govt is also keen to allow input tax credit on insurance, use of vehicles and other services. "ITC should be allowed in case of supplies, such as supply of passenger motor vehicle, leasing, repair, renting of motor vehicles, health and life insurance, outdoor catering, construction of telecommunication tower and pipelines, free samples and expired goods - as all are used in the furtherance of business," said Sameer Gupta, who leads the EY India tax practice.
This will come along with changes that will allow businesses to claim credit for taxes paid during the entire process even if some entities in the chain have not complied. "Invoice matching system now links what a seller reports with what a buyer claims, and mapping of input and output ledgers with the summary return completes the link. This is a major shift in how GSTN system works. Fake credit can be identified close to where it arises and stopped before it travels down the chain. The system provides the protection the condition was intended to provide," an official said.

briefs.headline: ‘System already straining’: Global oil buffers shrink amid mounting supply risks, say industry leaders
briefs.bodyText:
The global oil market is entering the winter with a much thinner safety cushion after more than 1 billion barrels were taken out of commercial stockpiles during this year's supply disruptions, industry executives said at a London energy conference.
The concern is not simply how much oil is sitting in storage, but how much of it can actually reach the market. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said less than 6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain globally, with only 10% or less considered practically available.
“Less than 6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain today, with the vast majority not practically available, so the system is already straining,” Nasser said at the Energy Intelligence Forum, as quoted by Reuters.
Oil can be counted as inventory without being immediately usable. Some crude is effectively tied up in pipelines or tank bottoms, while governments keep emergency reserves that cannot routinely be tapped. This leaves a much smaller pool of barrels that traders can access when supply suddenly falls.
That is becoming a bigger concern as global oil consumption is running at about 102 million barrels a day, according to the International Energy Agency. 
With fewer readily available barrels in storage, another major disruption could have a larger impact on prices.
Why inventories have been drained
Governments and energy companies have been relying on stored oil to compensate for supply disruptions linked to the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. More than 1 billion barrels have been released, mainly from commercial inventories, since the latest Middle East crisis began, Nasser said.
The drawdown has effectively used up much of the buffer that normally helps the market absorb temporary supply shocks. Rebuilding those stocks could take years because producers would have to add oil to storage while continuing to meet everyday global demand.
Chevron CEO Mike Wirth said the loss of these buffers had made the oil market more fragile and increased the price floor for crude.
The reduced cushion also leaves the market increasingly dependent on supplies that are still flowing, particularly seaborne exports from the Middle East. Vitol CEO Russell Hardy said there were few additional inventories left in Western markets that could be drained to make up for a fresh shortfall.
The US is also entering the period with a much smaller emergency crude cushion. Stocks in the country's Strategic Petroleum Reserve have fallen to their lowest level since October 1982, according to Department of Energy data.
The reserve is designed to provide additional crude during major supply disruptions, meaning its depleted
IEA plans 100 million-barrel release
The IEA is preparing to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel as it seeks to ease pressure in the market, particularly on diesel prices.
Nasser said the decision followed negotiations over how much oil could realistically be made available. It is not yet clear how much of the planned release will consist of barrels from the IEA's record 400 million-barrel release in March that had not yet reached the market.
The fresh release highlights the limited availability of emergency supplies. “Inventories are reaching a stress level. Only 10% or less is available,” Nasser said.
The intervention could provide some near-term relief, but executives at the London forum warned that replenishing depleted inventories would remain a challenge.

briefs.headline: Harness engineering is how AI developers are now trying to make agents work reliably | Explained
briefs.deck: As AI agents become more capable in 2026, developers are building systems around models to keep them on track, within boundaries and accountable for their actions
briefs.bodyText:
The story so far: For the past few years, improving AI largely meant improving what the model was told and what it could see. Prompt engineering emerged as a way of giving models better instructions. As tasks grew more complex, the focus expanded to context engineering, giving a model the right information at the right point rather than simply giving it more information.
AI agents take this a step further. An agent can plan a task, use software tools, retrieve information and take actions, rather than simply generate an answer for a person to act on. This means developers have to consider not just what the model knows, but what it can access, what it is allowed to do and how its work is checked. This is where harness engineering comes in.

stories.headline: The Asiad champs who made limited govt support count
stories.deck: India's remarkable performance, securing 21 gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, showcases the extraordinary talent of athletes who triumphed largely on meager resources. Archers Kumkum Mohod and Sahil Jadhav exemplify this feat, earning a mere Rs 50,000 through the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). Their success story, alongside other boxers and sailors, underscores the determination…
stories.bodyText:
New Delhi: India’s 21-gold campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has thrown up an interesting set of numbers: champions who reached the continental podium despite receiving relatively modest targeted financial assistance under the govt’s elite-athlete programmes.
Their stories do not diminish the broader support extended to Indian sport. Instead, they underline how performances can sometimes run ahead of the funding pipelines designed to identify and back medal prospects.
The clearest example is 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod. A recently-inducted Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) athlete for the Aich-Nagoya preparatory cycle, Kumkum became the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve gold at the Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 after a shoot-off. She also won gold in the women’s recurve team event and silver in mixed team, ending the campaign with three medals and securing India an LA Olympics quota.
The funding support extended to her puts her targeted assistance at just Rs 50,000. That is a striking figure against the scale of her achievement, even though her preparation also benefited from the budget allocated to the respective national sports federations (NSFs) under the Annual Calendar for Training and Competition (ACTC).
The same pattern is visible in compound archery. Sahil Rajesh Jadhav, who helped India win mixed team gold with Chikitha Taniparthi and also contributed to the men’s team gold, received Rs 50,000 under TOPS during the Games cycle. His top podium finish also delivered India an Olympic quota in compound archery.
Kushal Dalal and Thirumuru Ganesh Maniratnam, members of India’s men’s compound team that defeated China for gold, also received only Rs 50,000 each under TOPS during the cycle. Yet the trio of Dalal, Ganesh and Jadhav produced one of India’s five archery gold medals at the Games.
The contrast becomes sharper when placed alongside athletes receiving substantially larger targeted allocations. Boxer Ankush Panghal, for instance, received Rs 75,000 under TOPS, while his other gold partners in boxing Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda received Rs 22.97 lakh and Rs 8.59 lakh assistance, respectively, during the Games cycle.
These figures show that support was available at markedly different levels depending on an athlete’s classification, requirements, and timing within the system.
Similarly, in sailing, Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma secured the bronze medal in the women’s skiff, with both athletes not being part of the TOPS programme. Also, in the same sport, sailors Manu Francis and Prince Noble won silver in the men’s skiff, but both were not part of either TOPS Core or Development group. Boxer Kapil Pokhariya, too, wasn't part of the TOPS.
In shooting, the trio of Manisha Keer, Neeru Dhanda and Aashima Ahlawat won the silver medal in Trap women's team event, with Manisha receiving no TOPS assistance while Neeru, a TOPS Development athlete, getting Rs one lakh. In athletics, silver-wining javelin thrower Yashvir Singh wasn't part of the TOPS funding and largely prepared through the ACTC budget. In kurash, bronze-winner Pincky Balhara, competing in the -78 kg event, received Rs 75,000 under the TAGG scheme during the Games cycle.

Boxing: Ankush (Rs 75,000), Kapil Pokhariya (not covered under TOPS); 
Shooting: Neeru Dhanda (Rs 1,00,000), 
Kurash: Pincky Balhara (Rs 75,000), 
Athletics: Seema (Rs 25,000), Baranica Elangoan and Yashvir Singh (both not covered under TOPS).

stories.headline: Messi retires from international football as Argentina defeat Benin in friendly match
stories.deck: The 39-year-old, widely regarded as the greatest player in football history, had announced his decision to retire in August following Argentina’s World Cup defeat to Spain
stories.bodyText:
Lionel Messi retired from international football on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), scoring a goal and providing two assists as Argentina defeated Benin 3-0 in a friendly international.
Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolas Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring. Messi’s 71st minute penalty was his record-extending 126th international goal.
The 39-year-old, widely regarded as the greatest player in football history, had announced his decision to retire in August following Argentina’s World Cup defeat to Spain.
Messi brought the curtain down on his 21-year international career on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), bidding farewell to adoring Argentina fans in an emotional final appearance.
The match was a footnote to the occasion itself, which saw Messi savoring the adulation of the Monumental Stadium crowd one last time for an event which had been billed as ‘The Last Tango’.
Emotion and tears
Beforehand, Messi wiped away tears as the bus carrying him and his Argentina team-mates made its way through crowds of wellwishers en route to the stadium.
Messi took the field alongside his three children and received affectionate waves from his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, who were watching from a VIP box.
Shortly before kick off, a giant Argentina jersey bearing the word “Gracias” (Thank You) above the football superstar’s No.10 was laid out on the pitch as the crowd roared their approval.
Messi welled up again as Falklands War veteran Fabio Santana sang the national anthem beside a banner which read — “The Malvinas are Argentine” — the same banner held aloft by players after their 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England.
The match was halted in the 10th minute — in tribute to Messi’s famous shirt number — for a minute-long ovation to the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star.
He crowned the occasion with a goal from the penalty spot in the 71st minute.
‘Gave it my all’
At the final whistle a drone show lit up the night sky above the stadium, showing Messi’s image and thanking the eight-time Ballon D’Or-winner for his career.
Messi’s farewell came two and a half months after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression in an ill-tempered 1-0 loss.
“I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” Messi wrote at the time.
Before Tuesday’s game, the University of Buenos Aires awarded Messi an honorary doctorate in a ceremony at the Argentine Football Association (AFA) headquarters.
Messi, who has in the past spoken of his regret at not studying more, expressed pride at the distinction.
“To be able to say that I am an honorary doctor!,” he joked.
Outside the Argentina Football Association headquarters, fans unfurled a huge Argentine flag with his image inscribed “The joy of my life.”
Former Barcelona team-mate Neymar paid tribute to the departing champion on X.
“It’s not just Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football. Thank you for making me love football even more,” he said.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
Messi’s departure comes four years after his greatest triumph in international football, leading Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup to end the country’s 36-year wait for a third title, cementing his status as Diego Maradona’s heir.
“I believe Messi gave everything, absolutely everything, so it doesn’t bother me at all that he’s leaving. He has more than earned it, let him enjoy himself, let him rest,” Cecilia Adriano, 52, told AFP.
During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina won one World Cup, were runners-up twice (Brazil 2014 and North America 2026) and were also crowned Copa America champions in 2021 and 2024.

stories.headline: IND vs WI first T20I: Shreyas makes it a cakewalk for India
stories.deck: The skipper smashes his maiden T20I century as the Men in Blue romp home with 32 balls to spare
stories.bodyText:
Coming into the series opener, Shreyas Iyer was under some pressure, having not scored a half-century in his last 10 T20I appearances. All that changed on Tuesday as the Indian skipper slammed a sensational maiden T20I century, an unbeaten 102 (43b, 10x4, 6x6), to power the Men in Blue to a thumping eight-wicket win over the West Indies at the Ekana Stadium in Lucknow.
Chasing 172, India found itself in trouble at 35 for two after losing openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson cheaply.
With the match finely poised, Shreyas took charge in the final over of the PowerPlay, smashing Shamar Joseph for a hat-trick of boundaries to signal his intentions.
The Mumbai batter’s strength has always been his ability to find boundaries while playing orthodox shots. He unsettled the West Indies bowlers by shuffling in the crease to access acute angles.
In the ninth over, he did that repeatedly to Romario Shepherd, lofting the medium-pacer over covers for three back-to-back hits to the fence. At the other end, Ishan Kishan chipped in with a few boundaries, but he only had to put his captain back on strike, which he duly did.
Once he got past his half-century, which came off 28 balls, Shreyas cut loose, taking just 15 deliveries for the next 52 runs. Against Akeal Hosein, he backed away and lofted the left-arm spinner for a six and four over cover.
In the 14th over, Shreyas plundered 23 off Matthew Forde, including three maximums. The skipper deposited Roston Chase down the ground to bring up his ton and then sealed the win with 5.2 overs to spare.
Spinners excel
Earlier, the Indian tweakers led by debutant Naman Dhir (three for 31) wreaked havoc through the middle phase of the innings, scalping seven wickets to bundle West Indies out for 171.
For Windies, Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford did the heavy lifting, scoring fighting half-centuries.
While Hope got the team off to a strong start, the host pulled it back in the final over of the PowerPlay when Axar Patel (two for 26) bowled a maiden which included the wicket of Rovman Powell after the run-out of Shimron Hetmyer.
From 44 for three, Hope and Rutherford consolidated through a 63-run fourth-wicket stand. Dhir and Kuldeep (two for 33) then ran through the middle-order as the visitor slumped from 107 for three to 135 for eight.
Rutherford, though, got his team to a respectable total, punishing some poor bowling from the Indian quicks in the death overs, but against a rampaging Shreyas it was too little.

stories.headline: Ronaldo Explains Portugal Exit: Star details broken promises; vows return
stories.deck: Cristiano Ronaldo has revealed why he left Portugal’s camp, claiming Jorge Jesus broke promises over his playing time and then contradicted their private agreement publicly. Ronaldo said the situation left him feeling unwanted and that continuing would harm the team. He apologised for leaving, accepted responsibility for his actions and insisted he remains available to compete for Portugal after…
stories.bodyText:
Cristiano Ronaldo
 has finally explained why he walked away from the Portugal camp, delivering the detailed account he promised when the dispute with Jorge Jesus first erupted. The 41-year-old had said he would tell the Portuguese people what really happened “in due time”, and that moment has now arrived, with Ronaldo setting out the conversations that preceded his departure, the promises he says were made to him, the press conference that changed everything and the reasons he ultimately decided to leave.
Ronaldo had played in Portugal's 1-0 Nations League victory over Wales before becoming an unused substitute in the following 2-1 win against Norway, despite warming up for around 30 minutes. Jesus later explained that he had considered bringing Ronaldo onto the pitch but decided against it, while an emergency meeting involving Ronaldo, the Portugal coach and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença took place afterwards.
That meeting did not settle the dispute, and Ronaldo left the Portugal camp ahead of the team's 4-2 victory against Denmark. At the time, he issued a short statement saying that he would eventually reveal the reasons behind his decision, while Portugal continued their campaign without him and went on to win all four of their Nations League matches, taking 12 points from 12 and becoming the first team to secure qualification for the quarter-finals.
Jesus subsequently gave his own account after Portugal's 2-1 victory over Norway, saying Ronaldo remained eligible for selection and that the decision over whether he returned belonged entirely to the player.
Ronaldo has now provided his version of events in a lengthy statement posted across his social media channels, taking the story from the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup through to his decision to leave the Portugal camp. The statement comes with Ronaldo back at Al-Nassr, where he has already returned to training following his departure from the national team and is preparing to resume club football.
Ronaldo's full statement
"As I promised, I have decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances surrounding the latest stage of the national team's journey.
After the 2026 World Cup, I prepared a message for the Portuguese people, which I still keep, containing the words I would like to address to them when I finally leave our team.
At the end of the tournament, on the return flight from the United States, the federation president asked me and insisted that I reconsider my decision to leave, because the Portuguese Football Federation wished for me to continue.
Immediately afterwards, he asked me for my opinion on the name of the current national team coach, whom he was considering, alongside other names he did not reveal to me.
I answered the federation president that, in my opinion, it would be the ideal choice. Therefore, on the day the current national team coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with this choice. It was the right choice, as the results prove.
A few days later, I received the first call from the new national team coach, in which he said he wished to meet me in person. I answered in the affirmative, and we set a date for it. "The end of my holiday."
We met at the football city where my team was holding its pre-season training camp.
On that day the coach told me that he was counting on me and that my presence was essential to his project. He presented me with a plan for my immediate participation. He said I would play the first and last matches, and that he would make three or four changes in each match for reasons related to physical fitness.
At that point, he suggested that I not travel with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He suggested that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then join them before the match at the Dragão stadium.
I rejected this suggestion immediately. It seemed clear to me that I could not accept it. Not playing the matches abroad would not mean that I would not be captain of our team. The privilege of staying in Portugal would not set a good example.
In the end, the coach agreed with my analysis.
This conversation was attended by Simo Coutinho, the sporting director of Al-Nassr club, the person to whom the current national team coach reported throughout last season, and one of those responsible for his joining the club in 2025.
On the eve of the training camp, the coach came to my home in Lisbon to have another conversation with me at his request. The conversation was calm, and we adhered to all the principles agreed upon in August. I played the match at the Alvalade stadium, and despite being substituted, I caused no problems. I personally placed the captain's armband on Bruno Fernandes, and it never occurred to me that I might be taking my last steps as a player and captain of the national team. The most important thing that day, for me, was our win. Winning is always a good thing, and in Portugal, and for my country, it is the best.
At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, the national team coach's assistant came to the table where the team was having lunch, and told me that the coach wanted to talk to me. To my great surprise, the coach asked me whether I was ready to play 30 minutes. I was fully focused on my physical recovery, blending in with my teammates as usual, and believing I would not play that day. No problem at all.
This request was outside my physical recovery and training plan, because I was only going to play on the fourth of the month at the Dragão stadium, but of course I agreed. He answered me that I should be ready because I would play 30 minutes.
The rest is well known. I began warming up from half-time, and I watched the minutes pass, and no one called me on. The coach broke his promise.
At the end of the match, I only wanted everything to end with a win and to be alone. I did not go to greet the fans. A mistake I take responsibility for alone, and one that should not have happened. I apologise to the Portuguese people who supported us enthusiastically there, I apologise to the fans, and I apologise to those who travelled there to see me, even if they were not Portuguese, and whom I may have let down.
Forty-eight hours later, we had a conversation, myself, the coach and Simo Coutinho, because he was following our conversations
It was a very deep and frank moment, without any reservation.
We agreed that there was only one way to end this "case": that the coach would repeat what he had just told me in private, in the presence of Simo Coutinho, but in the press conference room.
The agreement was simple: the coach would begin the press conference with this subject, trying to end the matter by telling the truth. He would say that I had never asked to play even for a few minutes, and that the coach alone, no one else, was the one who proposed the plan for this training camp, and that it had been a mistake to subject me only to the warm-up without playing, and that, if it happened again, he would not do it.
We ended that meeting with the coach asking me for a hug, and he promised me that he would say in the press conference what he had just told me, and that the matter had been resolved. I would not play in Denmark, but I would play in the Dragão match. All of this took place in the presence of Simo Coutinho, as usual.
At the coach's request, a video meeting was held between him, Simo Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro, to summarise what we had discussed.
A brief document was prepared, which I personally approved, and it was handed to the coach at his request.
The meeting was as expected: the behaviour had nothing to do with our meeting. I heard expressions and aggression that I consider unjustified, and an attitude suggesting that he "wants, can, and orders" that he had never shown me, not even indirectly, in a private session, the day before.
The notes I reviewed were as follows: I believe it is important, because it is the truth, to clarify some matters before talking about Denmark:
- I personally proposed a plan for Cristiano, without anyone else, for this sporting season with the national team. It was a long and very fruitful conversation.
- I know how much he loves the national team and his global standing, and more than that, how positive his influence has been on the national team over 24 consecutive years.
- The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted.
- He never questioned my choices. He was an example to be followed, loyal, and professional.
- The Norway match was not included in the plan I had set for him. However, I felt that he had physically recovered from the first match, and I warned him that I might be forced to bring him on. Cristiano agreed.
- I made a mistake by involving a player of the magnitude of Pelé or Maradona only in the warm-up without involving him in the match. If it were today, I would not do that.
- In short: I want Cristiano in the national team. In truth, I do not want a little, I want a lot. And fortunately, he also trusts me. He believed in me at Al-Nassr and here too.
- As for not greeting the fans, we spoke about this matter earlier. A player who has played more than 230 matches with the national team does not take lessons from me in loving Portugal. It was a moment of frustration that erases nothing. He is the player who signs the most, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let us not create problems out of nothing. When we are not happy, we react. That is all there is to it. 
None of these notes, therefore, mentioned that the coach had apologised to me.
This was the second time he broke his promise.
I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for another promise that would not be kept. For me, the truth remains the most important thing in relationships between people. However painful it may be, I want the truth to be told to me.
In fact, in a conversation I had with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation and the coach on the morning of that press conference, you can verify this, I assured them that if they did not want my presence, they should tell me so. They only had to be frank with me. I would have accepted it and promised them that we would prepare something wonderful, as I hope will happen, and no one would be angry.
I remember it as if it happened yesterday. They answered with one voice in unison. assuring that my place is in the national team.
I have never intervened, at any time, in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team official throughout nearly 25 years of my career. I accept, whether it is good or bad, what they propose. I respect the decision, and when they break their promise to me, I feel that my place is not here.
I also apologise to my national team teammates for leaving the training camp. For despite my complete breach of the coach's trust, as everyone who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done that. The responsibility rests on me alone.
I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of my promise had a profound effect on me. I felt that my continuing with the team, from that moment, would only harm it, so I did what I always said I would do if I did not feel I was of use: I packed my bags and left.
The Portuguese Football Federation must assess the consequences of my actions and punish me for them. I believe the penalty should not be reduced. I am not just an ordinary player; I am the captain of the team, and that is an aggravating factor. I have already apologised, but I know that actions have consequences. Anyone in the world of football, like me, knows that the rules are the same for everyone, regardless of individual standing.
In this regard, I have heard a lot about farewell matches, and that I need a farewell befitting me, and that the federation wishes to grant me this opportunity.
I learned in life, while suffering from hunger and having nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone for free. I can promise all my fans, and especially the Portuguese people, that we will play one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.
But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competition. That is what I thought of on the day I received the news of my father's death. I was at a training camp with our national team, and I decided to stay there until the end of the next day's match. I did for my country what I would never have done for any club.
So, if I am physically fit, playing for my club and, hopefully, scoring goals, after serving whatever suspension that will be imposed on me, I will be available, as I always have been, to compete and win with our national team.
This, believe me, is the absolute truth."
Cristiano Ronaldo,
6 October 2026

briefs.headline: Back to the future: lessons from the Asian Games for the Olympics
briefs.deck: An Olympic medal will mean less to a player than winning a World Cup or World Test Championship. And if the games are in a country with little or no interest in cricket, it is unlikely to spread its message which is what the ICC hopes for
briefs.bodyText:
India were in a familiar situation at the Asian Games. Victory was taken for granted, defeat would have counted as a disgrace. This is the fate of top-ranked teams: damned if you do and doubly damned if you don’t.
The repercussions would have been greater had India lost to Japan following the infamous ‘wide ball’ in the last over by Axar Patel. The right decision was made, but it needed a show of dissent by the players to get there.
That an international tournament was played without DRS (and even, as it turned out, without proper pitches) is stunning. Forget the complaints about accommodation and transport, the fact that cricket had been reduced to a ritual doesn’t speak well of the International Cricket Council which should insist on minimum standards at multi-event games. One hopes the ICC (or its representative) will do better at the Olympic Games two years from now in Los Angeles where the teams and competition will be of a higher standard.
The final had one message for cricket fans: Know the ‘passport names’ of your heroes. Thus we learnt — thanks to the amateurish television coverage — that Sanju Samson was actually Sanju Viswanath in disguise, and that the man we have been admiring as Tilak Varma is in reality Tilak Namboori. Skipper Shreyas Santosh is rumoured to have been amused by it all.
It was a great match for nostalgia buffs. Often we missed the first ball of an over or the last, and had to sit through inane advertisements to find out if a batter had been dismissed and if so how so? We were back in the 1980s, with the Justice Lodha Commission recommendations (“advertisement should be telecast to the extent of drinks and break session and unnecessary advertisement after every over and fall of wicket should be avoided”) decades into the future.
Target audience?
It does raise a fundamental question: for whom is cricket played? The players, who have a personal stake in doing well, and who, presumably love what they are doing and can do things the rest of us can only fantasise about? The spectators, who buy into the tribal and cultural ethos without being conscious of these? The administrators, who enjoy the power and the positive impact on their business interests? Television moguls whose scorecard doesn’t have bowling or batting figures but dollar and cent signs? Columnists, who find the negatives in a positive and vice versa? Perhaps it is all of the above, some of the above or none of the above.
What Joyce Carol Oates said about boxing applies equally to cricket (or any sport at the highest level). Speaking of the three Ali-Frazier fights, she said these were “boxing’s analogues to King Lear – ordeals of unfathomable human courage and resilience raised to the level of classical tragedy.”
Still, India may have scored more runs and claimed more wickets in the tournament than viewers actually saw live, which takes us into the realm of philosophy. Does it count as a six or a wicket when no one saw it? TV can make philosophers of us all.
The Asian Games gives breath once again to the argument against having cricket in multi-event games like the Olympics. An Olympic medal will mean less to a player than winning a World Cup or World Test Championship. And if the games are in a country with little or no interest in cricket, it is unlikely to spread its message which is what the ICC hopes for. From the International Olympic Committee’s point of view, it will draw in the south Asian population, or more specifically, the television viewership (this will also call for more professional handling from TV).
Perhaps an age limit like in Olympic football (under-23) can be applied to cricket too. The argument is similar: a world cup exists already and a team would prefer to win that over an Olympic medal.
If the Asian Games cricket, which has asked more questions than provided answers, succeeds in raising the right questions ahead of the Olympic Games, then the telecast would be a minor crib. The ICC will have to find the balance between spreading the game and keeping the television viewership satisfied without diminishing the quality.

briefs.headline: Fenesta Open: Prabodh stuns Balsekar; top-seeded Sureshkumar-Sinha advance to quarterfinals
briefs.deck: The doubles competitions also got underway, with top seeds Manish Sureshkumar/Nitin Sinha advancing to the quarterfinals with a 7-5, 6-2 win over Raghav Jaisinghani/Lakshit Sood
briefs.bodyText:
Suraj Prabodh rallied from a set down to stun second seed Aditya Balsekar at the 31st Fenesta Open National Tennis Championship on Tuesday (October 6, 2026).
The 31-year-old Prabodh beat Balsekar 3-6, 6-2, 7-6 (7-4) at the DLTA Complex.
After losing the opening set, Prabodh adopted a more aggressive approach, a strategy that eventually paid dividends.
"Everybody knows he is a great player," Prabodh told the media after his win.
"I was just trying to hang in there and especially after the first set, I thought because he was too consistent and he was just everywhere. I thought I should just try to be a little more aggressive and get into the points or start the points a little more aggressively. Somehow I got through it and it was well planned and the execution was also perhaps better."
Fifth seed Oges Jaya was also knocked out in the first round, losing 7-5, 2-6, 6-4 to big-serving Raghav Jaisinghani. Fourth seed Udit Kamboj, however, avoided an upset with a 6-1, 7-5 win over rising youngster Aditya Mor.
In the women's singles draw, fifth seed Aditi Rawat, seventh seed Laxmi Siri Dandu, and eighth seed Sohini Mohanty registered wins. Rawat was made to work hard before prevailing 6-3, 7-5 over L Arunkumar.
“In the last game, honestly, I was just focusing on myself,” she said.
“I was trying to just go for my shots. I wasn't really concerned about the scoreboard or the score. I just tried to give my best in the match.”
The doubles competitions also got underway, with top seeds Manish Sureshkumar/Nitin Sinha advancing to the quarterfinals with a 7-5, 6-2 win over Raghav Jaisinghani/Lakshit Sood.
“It was a pretty good match,” Sureshkumar said after the win.
"I think there are a lot of good points. Hopefully our combination works going forward and let's see how it goes.”
Sinha credited his partner, who is also the top seed in the men’s singles draw, for the win. “He covered everything and it's always fun playing with him and we are looking forward to the next rounds.”
There was another big upset in the men’s doubles draw, with Aryan Chauhan/Karan Singh combining to knock out second seeds Madhwin Kamath/Rohan Mehra 6-3, 3-6, 10-7.
In the boys’ U-18 draw, top seed Praneel Sharma scored a 6-0, 6-3 win over Sarthak Gaikwad to reach the round of 16. Third seed Harsh Malik was upset in the second round, while fourth seed Om Patel, and fifth seed Mor, also advancing to the last 16.
In the girls’ U-18 draw, top seed S Bhuvaneswaran and third seed Shreeniti Chowdhury scored comfortable wins to reach the third round.

briefs.headline: India’s fight fades as Uruguay nets six
briefs.deck: The visitors show their might in the second half after Thapa makes it 1-1 in the 22nd minute; the host struggles to maintain its defensive discipline
briefs.bodyText:
India showed enough attacking intent to suggest it could compete with two-time world champion Uruguay, but a second-half collapse exposed the gulf in pace, depth and efficiency as the host eventually capitulated to a 1-6 loss at the Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday (October 6, 2026).
India started positively but struggled to maintain its defensive discipline as the game progressed.
Uruguay took the lead in the 11th minute when Federico Vinas was brought down inside the box, allowing Darwin Nunez to convert from the spot.
Responding well
India responded well and drew level in the 22nd minute. Ryan Williams’ effort was parried by goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo, but Thapa reacted quickest to the rebound and fired home.
The Blue Tigers were able to find openings in the final third whenever they moved the ball with purpose.
But their vulnerability was exposed when possession changed hands. That weakness was evident in the 28th minute after play resumed following a 35-minute delay due to lightning.
Rodrigo Bentancur released Nandez down the right as India failed to reorganise quickly enough, allowing the full-back to find Maxi Araujo, who produced a clinical finish to put Uruguay in the lead.
The goal highlighted India’s biggest problem: it lacked the speed to shift from attack to defence and struggled to rebuild quickly after winning possession.
There were encouraging moments, too. Gurpreet Singh Sandhu produced an excellent 37th-minute save to deny Nunez after the striker had been put through.
India went into the break 1-2 down, with its attacking players — Edmund Lalrindika, Manvir Singh and Williams — lacking precision in the final third.
Uruguay coach Diego Forlan made seven changes, including Lucas Torreira and Facundo Pellistri, adding fresh quality and energy to his side. Rodrigo Zalazar made it 3-1 in the 53rd minute, Araujo scored his second in the 59th, Juan Sanabria found the target in the 71st, and Rodrigo Aguirre netted in the 86th to complete the rout.
India’s efforts did not disappear, but its inability to match Uruguay’s pace and intensity became increasingly evident.
The host struggled to close spaces and recover its defensive shape as Uruguay repeatedly exploited transitions.
India had late opportunities through substitutes Mohammed Sanan and Sahal Abdul Samad, but both efforts were saved by Cardozo in the Uruguay goal.
The result: India 1 (Anirudh Thapa 22) lost to Uruguay 6 (Darwin Nunez 11-pen, Maxi Araujo 28, 59, Rodrigo Zalazar 53, Juan Sanabria 71, Rodrigo Aguirre 86).

briefs.headline: India vs New Zealand T20I series: Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns after four-year gap
briefs.deck: India will be playing New Zealand in the five-match T20I series from October 22, 2026.
briefs.bodyText:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return to India’s T20I squad after nearly four years will be one of the talking points of the forthcoming tour of New Zealand, starting October 22.
The 36-year-old last represented India in November 2022. His recall — rewarded for his performances in Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s back-to-back IPL triumphs — comes as the four-member selection panel, in the presence of BCCI Centre of Excellence head of cricket V.V.S. Laxman, sought to balance immediate T20I requirements with the demands of a long multi-format New Zealand tour.
India will play five T20Is, beginning in Christchurch on October 22, with Shreyas Iyer continuing as captain and Tilak Varma as his deputy.
The selectors have simultaneously kept an eye on the longer formats. Washington Sundar, who was withdrawn from the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies, will instead play three First Class matches for India-A in New Zealand.
Rishabh Pant has also been included in the India-A squad, subject to fitness. The wicketkeeper-batter, who batted well down the order in the second innings of the Irani Cup, has been asked to play the multi-day fixtures as part of his return to full fitness.
Yashasvi Jaiswal, K.L. Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal and B. Sai Sudharsan headline the India-A batting group while Dhruv Jurel has been named captain.
R. Smaran and Yash Rathod have been persisted with for their impressive run with the willow. Akash Deep, who returned to competitive cricket after seven months during the Irani Cup tie, has been included in the India-A squad along with Mukesh Kumar, Mukesh Choudhary and Anshul Kamboj.
The BCCI said the squads for the ODI and Test series would be announced later.
The squads: T20Is: Shreyas Iyer (Capt.), Tilak Varma (Vice-capt.), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wk), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, and Kuldeep Yadav.
The fixtures: Oct. 22 and 24 (Christchurch), Oct. 27 (Wellington), Oct. 30 (Auckland), Nov. 1 (Hamilton).

*Subject to fitness

briefs.headline: Who is Anirudh Thapa, only the second Indian to score against Uruguay in 44 years?
briefs.deck: India’s 6–1 defeat to Uruguay was painful, but Anirudh Thapa provided a rare moment of history by ending the country’s 44-year wait for a goal against La Celeste. His rebound made him only the second Indian scorer against Uruguay, joining Manas Bhattacharya, who struck in 1982. For Thapa, the landmark goal also marked his first international strike since 2023.
briefs.bodyText:
India may have suffered a heavy 6–1 defeat to Uruguay in Kolkata, but one moment still gave the home crowd something significant to celebrate. Anirudh Thapa's equaliser against the two-time FIFA World Cup champions ended a 44-year wait for an Indian goal against La Celeste, placing the midfielder alongside a player from a very different era of the national team's history.
Anirudh Thapa ends India's 44-year wait against Uruguay
Thapa became only the second Indian footballer to score against Uruguay when he reacted quickest to a rebound and turned it into the equaliser during Tuesday's international friendly at the Salt Lake Stadium.
Uruguay had taken the lead in the 11th minute after Indian defender Pramveer was penalised for a foul inside the area, with former Liverpool forward Darwin Núñez converting the resulting penalty after sending Gurpreet Singh Sandhu the wrong way.
India responded just 11 minutes later, with Ryan Williams winning possession in midfield before carrying the ball forward and striking from the edge of the box.
Uruguay goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo managed to parry Williams' effort, but Thapa had followed the move closely and reacted first to the loose ball before calmly finishing from the rebound.
The goal briefly brought India level at 1–1 and gave the home side a huge lift against a Uruguay team ranked 20th in the world, with India sitting 138th.
It was also an important personal moment for Thapa, because the strike was his fifth international goal and his first for India since March 2023.
Uruguay eventually pulled away in the second half, with Maximiliano Araújo scoring twice while Rodrigo Zalazar, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Aguirre also found the net to complete a 6–1 victory.
Thapa's goal nevertheless secured his place in a very small piece of Indian football history.
Manas Bhattacharya was the first Indian to score against Uruguay
Before Thapa's rebound at the Salt Lake Stadium, the previous Indian goal against Uruguay had been scored 44 years earlier by Manas Bhattacharya.
Bhattacharya found the net during the 1982 Nehru Cup at Eden Gardens in Kolkata, although his goal could not prevent India from losing the match 3–1.
Uruguay had already built a two-goal advantage through Jorge da Silva before Bhattacharya pulled one back in the 35th minute.
The goal made Bhattacharya the first Indian to score against Uruguay, a distinction he held for more than four decades before Thapa joined him on Tuesday night.
Bhattacharya was a prominent winger during the 1970s and 1980s and earned a strong reputation during his spells with Mohun Bagan and Mohammedan Sporting.
India and Uruguay have only met twice previously, with Uruguay winning both encounters, although the second meeting came against a Uruguay B team during the 2001 Millennium Super Soccer Cup in Kochi.
That match ended 3–0 to Uruguay, meaning Thapa's strike was the first Indian goal against the South Americans since Bhattacharya's effort in Kolkata in 1982.
Who is Anirudh Thapa?
Thapa was born in Dehra Dun on January 15, 1998, and the 28-year-old has become one of the more established midfielders in Indian football after several years around the national-team setup.
He currently plays for Mohun Bagan Super Giant in the 
Indian Super League
 and has already won the ISL twice during his career, while making his senior India debut in 2017 and accumulating more than 60 international appearances.
His development began when he started playing football at the age of 10 with St. Stephen's Football Academy in Chandigarh.
Thapa then represented India's under-14 side before earning a place at the AIFF Regional Academy in Kalyani in 2012, later moving into the AIFF Elite Academy and eventually captaining the I-League under-19 team.
Kolkata: India's Anirudh Thapa, left, celebrates with Ryan Williams after scoring a goal during an International friendly Football match between India and Uruguay, in Kolkata. (PTI Photo/Manvender Vashist Lav)(PTI10_06_2026_000500B)
In 2016, he was one of four Indian players selected for an opportunity with French Ligue 2 club Metz, giving him an early taste of European football before he established himself domestically.
His Indian Super League journey began in 2016 when Chennaiyin FC signed him, followed by a loan move to Minerva Punjab after the 2018 ISL season.
Thapa made his debut for Minerva Punjab against Mohun Bagan in January 2017 before returning to Chennaiyin in May that year when his loan spell ended.
After the 2021–22 ISL season, Thapa left Chennaiyin and joined Mohun Bagan, where he continued developing as one of India's established midfield options.
His goal against Uruguay now gives that career another notable chapter, because despite India's eventual 6–1 defeat, Thapa has become only the second Indian player ever to find the net against the two-time world champions.

briefs.headline: ‘We won't be marking Messi’: Benin defender’s message ahead of icon’s farewell
briefs.deck: Benin defender Mohamed Tijani has shared his respect for Lionel Messi before his final international match. Argentina will face Benin in a friendly, marking Messi's farewell in the national team. Tijani emphasised that the focus will be on enjoying the occasion rather than stopping Messi. Messi's international career has been historic, leading Argentina to several achievements, including the…
briefs.bodyText:
Benin defender Mohamed Tijani has offered a heartwarming perspective ahead of Lionel Messi’s final international appearance for Argentina, saying his team will not man-mark the legendary forward but instead savour the opportunity to share the pitch with one of football’s greatest icons.
Argentina face Benin in a friendly at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, with the match set to mark Messi’s farewell in the famous blue-and-white shirt. The occasion has been billed as an emotional celebration of the 39-year-old’s extraordinary international career, with thousands of fans expected to turn out to bid farewell to their captain.
Speaking to Argentine outlet C5N ahead of the game, Tijani made it clear that stopping Messi would not be the only priority for Benin.
“We would not be marking Messi. We will just enjoy this match. I will watch him and say: Messi, you are a legend,” Tijani said, as quoted by Goal.com.
The Benin defender’s admiration for Messi goes even further. According to Goal.com, Tijani said he hoped Argentina would win the farewell match, despite his own side being the opposition.
“We will do our utmost to ensure this celebration is perfect,” Tijani said, speaking about Messi’s final international outing.
Messi’s final bow for Argentina
Messi announced his decision to retire from international football on September 1, following Argentina’s 0-1 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. He had previously retired from international duty in 2016 after Argentina lost the Copa America final to Chile, but reversed that decision and subsequently enjoyed the most successful period of his international career.
Messi led Argentina to Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024 before finally achieving his long-held dream of winning the World Cup in Qatar in 2022. Argentina defeated France on penalties in the final after a thrilling 3-3 draw.
His farewell comes after a record-breaking international career. Messi is Argentina’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player, having made 207 appearances and scored 125 goals for his country. He has also scored 21 goals across six World Cup appearances.
A farewell to remember
Messi’s final international appearance is expected to be an emotional occasion at the Monumental, where more than 85,000 supporters are set to witness the Argentine great take the field for one last time for his country.
The Argentine Football Association has described the occasion as one that will “transcend sports” and be filled with emotion. Messi himself reflected on the significance of the moment after joining up with the Argentina squad for the final time.
“Special moments I know I will miss,” Messi wrote on social media.
While his international career is coming to an end, Messi will continue playing club football for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.

briefs.headline: Shreyas Iyer's maiden T20I century powers India to eight-wicket win over West Indies
briefs.deck: In a thrilling opening match of the series, Shreyas Iyer reached his maiden T20I century, finishing with a stunning 102 runs off just 43 balls. This remarkable innings paved the way for India's eight-wicket triumph over West Indies. Debutant Naman Dhir made a mark too, claiming three wickets as the Windies were limited to 171 runs. India now leads the series 1-0, showcasing their prowess in both…
briefs.bodyText:
India skipper Shreyas Iyer marked his return to form in spectacular fashion, smashing his maiden T20I century as India cruised to an eight-wicket win over West Indies in the opening match of the five-match series on Tuesday.
Chasing 172, India raced to 172 for two in just 14.4 overs, with Iyer producing a breathtaking unbeaten 102 off 43 balls. The century, completed with a towering six off Roston Chase, was the fastest by an Indian batter against West Indies in T20Is.
Iyer walked off to a standing ovation after taking his helmet off and raising both hands towards the Indian dugout. His innings featured six sixes and a total of 10 boundaries.
The chase did not begin without a scare. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma added 15 runs in the opening over, but West Indies hit back through their spin duo of Akeal Hosein and Roston Chase, who dismissed both openers.
Iyer took charge alongside Ishan Kishan and turned the chase into a one-sided contest. The Indian skipper's assault ensured the hosts never allowed the required rate to become a concern.
Naman Dhir stars on debut
Earlier, debutant Naman Dhir delivered an impressive all-round performance with the ball, claiming three wickets as India bowled West Indies out for 171 in 19.1 overs.
Shai Hope top-scored for the visitors with a 37-ball 52, while Sherfane Rutherford provided the late impetus with a powerful 56 off 34 balls. West Indies made a brisk start, with Hope smashing Mayank Yadav for four boundaries in the second over. Arshdeep Singh then provided India with the first breakthrough by cleaning up Kamil Pooran.
The visitors' innings suffered another setback when Shimron Hetmyer was run out in the sixth over, before Axar Patel dismissed Rovman Powell for a duck. Rutherford briefly shifted the momentum back towards West Indies, taking on Kuldeep Yadav and Axar Patel during an aggressive 56. Hope also brought up a half-century before falling to Dhir in the 12th over.
India then tightened the screws. Kuldeep removed Roston Chase before Dhir struck twice more to finish with impressive figures of 3/31. Kuldeep returned 2/33, while Axar picked up 2/26.
With West Indies restricted to 171, Iyer ensured there was never any doubt about the result. His unbeaten century not only sealed India's eight-wicket victory but also gave the skipper the perfect start to the five-match series as India took a 1-0 lead.

briefs.headline: Anirudh Thapa goal a brief bright spot as Uruguay run riot against India
briefs.deck: India ended their three-match home friendly window with a 1-6 defeat to Uruguay at Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday. Anirudh Thapa's goal briefly gave the home faithfuls something to celebrate. But in a game of two halves, Uruguay found their scoring shoes with Darwin Nunez, Maxi Araujo, Rodrigo Zalazar, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Aguirre hitting the back of the net.
briefs.bodyText:
TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: India's third and final friendly test on home soil ended on a losing note as they went down 1-6 to Uruguay at the Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday. Anirudh Thapa's first half strike gave the home faithful something to celebrate in what was a heartening performance in the first half despite the scoreline. A Brace from Maxi Araujo coupled with goals from Rodrigo Zalazar, Darwin Nunez, Juan Manuel Sanabria and Rodrigo Aguirre put the game beyond India.
India held Panama to a 1-1 draw in Bengaluru in the first friendly of the FIFA international window. They were then swept aside 0-4 by Brazil on Saturday in Kolkata. The six goals conceded on Tuesday, in front of 37,307 fans, dampened what had been a promising start to the three important friendlies.
In a game that witnessed a lightning strike enforced 30-minute delay, Uruguay were far and above the better side in the second half to nullify India's solid first half showcase.
The promising start quickly unravelled as Uruguay capitalised on defensive lapses and moments of transition to secure a comprehensive win, their second of the tour of Asia, having earlier beaten South Korea.
India, meanwhile, had their moments, particularly in the opening stages, but Uruguay’s greater quality in the final third eventually told. 
The visitors repeatedly exposed gaps behind the Indian defence, with Maxi Araujo and Zalazar among those making the most of the opportunities presented to them.
India had the first meaningful opening in the fifth minute when Akash Mishra met a corner inside the box and attempted a left-footed strike, but his effort sailed over.
Edmund Lalrindika was then presented with an even better opportunity after India won possession high up the pitch. The ball fell to him with only the goalkeeper to beat, but he lacked composure and drifted wide before running out of room.
Uruguay were awarded a penalty soon after, with Pramveer adjudged to have brought down Federico Viñas inside the box. The decision was greeted with loud boos from the home crowd, who felt the Uruguay forward had gone down too easily. Darwin Nuñez made no mistake from the spot, sending Gurpreet Singh Sandhu the wrong way to give Uruguay the lead.
India's goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu fails to save a penalty by Uruguay's Darwin Nunez during the international friendly soccer match between India and Uruguay in Kolkata, India, Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Bikas Das)
The visitors almost doubled their advantage in the 16th minute. Nunez was sent through and, rather than shoot, cut the ball back for M. Araujo, whose curling effort beat Gurpreet but came back off the post.
India responded impressively and were level in the 22nd minute.
Ryan Williams found himself with plenty of space and, encouraged by the crowd, unleashed a shot that goalkeeper Thiago Cardozo could only spill. Anirudh Thapa reacted quickest, staying onside before producing a composed left-footed finish to make it 1-1.
India continued to threaten, with Williams again involved minutes later. He drove forward on the right and found Edmund in the centre, but after a couple of touches inside the box, the Indian forward was crowded out by the Uruguay defence.
The momentum was then interrupted by a thunderstorm. Play was stopped at 8:04pm, with players and staff sent back to the dressing rooms. After a 30-minute delay, as per FIFA's protocols revolving lightning, the match resumed.
Lightning brings play to a halt during India vs Uruguay at Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.
Uruguay needed just two minutes after the restart to regain the lead.
A cross from the right by Nandez caught India off guard. Ashique Kuruniyan attempted to step up, but the space he left allowed Nandez to exploit the opening, with Araujo finishing the move to put Uruguay 2-1 ahead.
Kolkata: Uruguay's Maximiliano Araujo, 20, celebrates after scoring a goal during an International friendly Football match between India and Uruguay, in Kolkata. (PTI Photo/Manvender Vashist Lav)(PTI10_06_2026_000648A)
India were increasingly vulnerable on the counter. Nunez was played through by Zalazar in the 37th minute and found himself completely clear, but his attempted chip was thwarted by Gurpreet, who stood tall and managed to get his body behind the effort.
After the half time break, Uruguay took complete control of the game.
Zalazar extended the lead in the 53rd minute after Nunez nodded the ball down into his path on the edge of the box. Zalazar took a touch before unleashing a powerful strike into the bottom corner, giving Gurpreet no chance.
Soccer Football - International Friendly - India vs Uruguay - Salt Lake Stadium, Kolkata, India - October 6, 2026 Uruguay's Rodrigo Zalazar celebrates scoring their third goal REUTERS/Sahiba Chawdhary
Araujo added his second of the night six minutes later. Viñas slipped a through ball behind the Indian defence and Araujo raced beyond the backline, shrugging off Abhishek Singh before calmly finishing past Gurpreet for 4-1.
Soccer Football - International Friendly - India vs Uruguay - Salt Lake Stadium, Kolkata, India - October 6, 2026 Uruguay's Maximiliano Araujo celebrates scoring their fourth goal REUTERS/Sahiba Chawdhary
India continued to look for a response. Gurpreet denied Zalazar at one end, while Apuia tried his luck from distance at the other, only to see his effort sail over.
Sanan briefly lifted the home crowd in the 69th minute, weaving past one defender before creating space for a long-range attempt. His lofted effort was punched over by the goalkeeper, prompting a huge roar from the stands.
But Uruguay immediately exposed India at the other end.
Another transition caught the hosts out and Sanabria finished at the far post to make it 5-1.
Kolkata: Uruguay's Juan Manuel, 25, scores a goal as India's Gurpreet Singh Sandhu looks on during an International friendly Football match between India and Uruguay, in Kolkata. (PTI Photo/Manvender Vashist Lav)(PTI10_06_2026_000687B)
The visitors added a sixth late on. Facundo Pellistri burst down the right before finding Aguirre in space on the edge of the box. Aguirre took a touch, wrong-footed Bijoy and curled a superb finish into the top corner, leaving substitute goalie Albino Gomes with no chance.
Soccer Football - International Friendly - India vs Uruguay - Salt Lake Stadium, Kolkata, India - October 6, 2026 Uruguay's Rodrigo Aguirre celebrates scoring their sixth goal with teammates REUTERS/Sahiba Chawdhary
Uruguay's 6-1 victory ultimately reflected the gulf between the sides in terms of ruthlessness and the ability to punish mistakes. India showed enough attacking intent to suggest there were positives to take, but their defensive organisation was repeatedly exposed whenever Uruguay accelerated the game.
